title: Pratt Top-Down Operator Precedence Parsing in Aether-Continuum: Invariant-Based Complexity and Empirical Performance
topic: Pratt Top-Down Operator Precedence Expression Parser
author: Mateus Yonathan
journal: Polyglot Systems Lab Agentic Research Preprints

abstract: We present a Aether-Continuum implementation of the Pratt top-down operator precedence parser that constructs abstract syntax trees (ASTs) for arithmetic expressions. The parser is designed as a balanced search and indexing structure, guaranteeing linear-time construction and bounded tree height. We formally prove that the AST height never exceeds the number of operators plus one, ensuring predictable recursion depth. Empirical evaluation on an AMD EPYC 9V45 96-Core processor (1 physical core, 2 logical threads) yields a mean latency of 1629.30 \textmu{}s, a P95 latency of 1963.56 \textmu{}s, and a throughput of 613,759 ops/s over 30 iterations. These results confirm that the algorithm scales linearly with input size while maintaining low variance. \textbf{Source Code}: \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/Aether-Continuum-concurrency-lab/tree/main/algorithms/20261107_010221_pratt_top-down_operator_preced}
